findings.text: Hepatic-impairment data are limited and no specific adjustment is supplied. Obtain individual consultant/pharmacy advice rather than an invented dose.

Coordinate invasive dental work with dentistry and oncology. Avoid close proximity to zoledronic acid where possible; evidence does not define a universal drug-holiday interval or prove that stopping eliminates ONJ risk.
Complete the indicated dental assessment, preventive care and individual benefit-risk review before treatment.
Resolve required renal, calcium, phosphate and magnesium results before the infusion. Baseline also includes FBC and liver profile; vitamin D and dental assessment are as clinically indicated.

Hypercalcaemia is an exception to routine calcium/vitamin D supplementation in this adjuvant source. Review the cause and supplementation; it does not convert this assessment into a hypercalcaemia-treatment regimen.
Confirm the prescribed calcium/vitamin D plan and whether hypercalcaemia alters it. NCCP specifies daily supplementation of at least 500 mg calcium and at least 400 IU vitamin D.
Individualise hydration and avoid overhydration with cardiac failure or fluid-overload risk; no routine echo schedule is specified for this regimen.
Review potentially nephrotoxic or calcium-lowering medicines and antiangiogenic therapy; these may increase renal, electrolyte or jaw-osteonecrosis risk.
Evaluate new thigh, hip or groin pain for an incomplete atypical femoral fracture and consider interruption while assessed; use the individual benefit-risk decision.
Investigate persistent ear symptoms, including possible external-auditory-canal osteonecrosis; no fixed dose reduction is specified.
Arrange prompt clinical/ophthalmic assessment of new eye pain or visual change; ocular inflammation is a recognised adverse effect.
Withhold and clinically assess renal deterioration or acute kidney injury even if a numerical trigger is not established.
Withhold pending dental/oral-surgery and oncology review for suspected osteonecrosis of the jaw or a significant dental concern; subsequent interruption and treatment are individualised.
Correct dehydration and reassess renal function before infusion; tailor fluids to the clinical situation.
Reconcile duplicate therapy before dosing: do not give another bisphosphonate or additional zoledronic-acid product concurrently.
Withhold and arrange urgent assessment for possible severe hypocalcaemia, including tetany, seizure or arrhythmia; do not wait for a routine repeat infusion.
Withhold and urgently assess severe systemic illness or a suspected serious infusion/allergic reaction. Do not assume fever or sudden illness is only an expected post-dose reaction.
Delay starting a new treatment course until unhealed open oral soft-tissue lesions have been assessed and healed; resolve the dental plan.
